Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G 6 PD) deficiency is primarily inherited in an
X-linked recessive pattern, which means that the gene responsible for this enzyme
deficiency is located on the X chromosome. As a result, males, who have only one X
chromosome, are more severely affected by the deficiency, often presenting with hemolytic
anemia when exposed to certain oxidative stressors. Females, possessing two X chromosomes,
may be carriers and display milder symptoms or none at all, owing to X-inactivation. This
genetic pattern has significant implications for affected populations, particularly in
areas where malaria is prevalent, as G 6 PD deficiency confers some protection against
severe malaria. Understanding the inheritance and population dynamics of G 6 PD deficiency
is crucial for public health strategies and genetic counseling.
answers.explanation: The answer correctly identifies the X-linked recessive inheritance pattern of G6PD deficiency, explaining its greater impact on males due to their single X chromosome and the potential for females to be carriers with milder or no symptoms, which highlights the genetic basis and implications for affected individuals and populations.
